The Attitudes Towards Internationalism & Federalism study is a result of two distinct surveys, one bearing on federalism which includes Canada, the United States, and Mexico, and the other on internationalism which relates to only Canada and the United States. The survey on federalism constitutes an annual evaluation of the attitudes of the public regarding federalism. Approximately 2,000 surveys were conducted in Mexico, 2,012 in Canada, and 1,004 in the United States of adults aged 18 and over
. This survey allows researchers to examine the similarities and differences between Canada, the United States, and Mexico in regards to some pertinent bureaucratic and social issues.

dct_spatial_sm: Canada, Mexico and the United States

This survey covers Canada, the United States, and Mexico. Canada is further sub-divided by province, the United States is further sub-divided by state, and Mexico is further sub-divided by state and then again by city.
